rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). However, most candidates lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC or PRS-only R²) and instead report full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r, limiting confident ranking. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with a clearly reported PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) under basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), providing more directly interpretable PRS evidence than candidates where the headline discrimination is full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS001784, PGS003429, PGS003972, PGS003973) or a weakly comparable partial correlation (PGS002054). Remaining limitation: PGS000753 uses a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and does not report PRS-only AUROC/R², while other models use genome-wide shrinkage methods and/or report covariates-regressed-out R² (PGS001784), so the evidence is insufficient to call a clearly best, high-quality winner.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/AUD): PGS002738 and PGS002739 are explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201 and PGS000202 are labeled "Problematic alcohol use" but their phenotyping_reported is also AUD (DSM-5 criteria count), making them concept-aligned direct matches. Among these, PGS002738 is best supported by endpoint fidelity (AUD), disease-focused multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB), and the strongest visible discrimination-style evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized European evaluation (n=7,900). However, the overall evidence remains limited for a high-confidence pick because none of the candidates report PRS-comparable AUC or R2, covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (reducing comparability), and the two 2020 siblings (PGS000201/PGS000202) provide only small incremental ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) without clearer PRS-only metrics, leaving some unresolved uncertainty in cross-model comparability.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis). PGS004913 has the strongest endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis, matching the target wording) and reports a PRS-comparable metric (R²=0.029) plus an OR (top vs bottom deciles)=4.4, with only basic covariates (age, sex, 10 PCs). PGS000704 reports only a full-model C-index=0.711 from a broader biomarker genetics paper and provides no PRS-only AUC/R²; its HR per SD=1.18 suggests modest PRS signal and the full-model metric is not directly comparable as PRS performance. PGS001777 is disease-focused but is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and its reported AUROC=0.671 is also a full-model metric; while it shows a large top-20% vs bottom-20% OR=6.18, the limited variant set and unclear modeling details reduce confidence. Overall, PGS004913 is best supported by coherent phenotype alignment and the presence of a PRS-comparable R², but confidence remains limited because none of the candidates provides a clearly reported PGS-only AUROC and cross-study metric comparability is constrained.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned phenotyping (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3 / time-to-event angina). Among models with explicit PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet pan-trait framework scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262; from “Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits in UK Biobank”) are penalized by domain guidance as likely to generalize poorly despite complete metrics. Within that sibling set, PGS001262 has the strongest reported discrimination evidence (PGS-only AUROC=0.58683; PGS R2=0.01304; incremental AUROC=0.0098; full-model AUROC=0.80729 with only basic covariates) and a directly stated doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint, making it the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. However, confidence is limited because the strongest-performing alternatives by effect size (e.g., PGS004527 OR=1.429) and several newer MVP-based PheCode models with high C-index (~0.76) lack clearly PRS-only metrics (and/or have non-comparable full-model metrics), preventing a clean, high-confidence ranking across study families.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but they come from different study archetypes and report non-comparable metrics. Among the EUR-evaluated options, PGS001267 provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.72651; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.09877) plus basic covariates and a large European validation sample (n=67,425), and its PRS R2 is plausibly below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.3993). Competing EUR models from the UKB portability paper (PGS001876, PGS002089) lack AUROC/R2 and only report partial correlation, limiting comparability; the EAS-only Taiwanese models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and have smaller validation (n=1,298), making them less generally supported without a specified deployment ancestry. Main limitation: PGS001267 is from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalization risk per domain guidance) and a near-twin time-to-event variant (PGS001268) has slightly higher full-model AUROC, so the evidence does not cleanly identify a single unequivocal best model.

Among the 8 returned models, four are not direct matches to the target trait (they are for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: PGS000739, PGS000778, PGS004910, PGS004911). The remaining four are aortic-stenosis–aligned: PGS005252 and PGS005254 have trait_reported/trait_efo of aortic stenosis with phenotyping_reported as incident aortic stenosis; PGS005255 and PGS005256 are labeled as aortic valve function measures (mean pressure gradient / peak aortic velocity) even though their phenotyping_reported is incident aortic stenosis, making them less endpoint-faithful than the explicit aortic stenosis models.

Between the two explicit aortic stenosis candidates, PGS005252 is better supported by the visible evidence because it provides a reported discrimination metric (C-index 0.87 in European validation) plus an effect size (HR 1.92), whereas PGS005254 provides only an HR (1.64) and no AUC/C-index. Both are EUR-only development/evaluation and both use incident AS endpoints; however, PGS005252’s covariate set is heavier (multiple clinical risk factors), so its high full-model C-index may be partly covariate-driven and is not a substitute for PRS-only performance—this limits confidence. Still, given the stronger available performance evidence and larger HR, PGS005252 is the best-supported direct-match choice from the provided context.

Direct-match candidates for the exact target trait are present (notably PGS001135: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate “Arthritis (nos)” / “arthritis”). This endpoint fidelity is stronger for the generic target “arthritis” than the many subtype-specific alternatives in the context (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, gout, osteoarthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis). However, the available performance evidence for PGS001135 suggests weak standalone PRS signal: it reports PGS-only AUROC 0.53928 and PGS R2 (no covariates) 0.00291, with very small incremental AUROC (0.00314), indicating limited added discrimination beyond covariates. Additionally, another direct-match option exists (PGS004477/PGS004547, “M13 (Other arthritis)” with trait_efo=arthritis) but provides only an OR without comparable PRS-only metrics, making it hard to justify over the exact “Arthritis (nos)” model. Therefore a direct match is available but evidence is insufficient for a clearly strong recommendation.

Multiple direct-match asthma PRS candidates are present. PGS002727 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment for asthma (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 985,837 variants), reports a comparatively strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) and a full-model AUROC of 0.66 with an R² of 0.04, and is evaluated in a very large sample (n=391,820) with multi-ancestry evaluation listed. Main limitation: the endpoint is pediatric-specific rather than generic asthma, and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability and making it unclear how much reported discrimination is PRS-driven versus covariate-driven; additionally, several other asthma models exist with similar or higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS001344 AUROC 0.666) but without clearly superior PRS-only metrics, leaving residual uncertainty.

All 6 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical (therapy-associated) eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients, which is not a generic atopic eczema endpoint; PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (subtype/severity-restricted) and reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with covariates, which domain guidance says is not a valid substitute for PRS-only metrics and is also implausibly high relative to the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.1288), suggesting covariate-driven performance or non-comparable reporting. The remaining endpoint-faithful options are PGS002755 and PGS004587, both using incident atopic dermatitis with similar covariates and large European evaluation (n=337,910). Between them, PGS002755 is structurally stronger (PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants vs 23 GWAS-significant SNPs) and shows a slightly higher HR (1.249 vs 1.153), supporting better PRS signal. However, confidence is limited because neither provides PRS-only AUROC/R² and both come from contexts where full-model discrimination is not reported, leaving comparability and absolute PRS performance uncertain.

Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in the provided context because it is a disease-focused, multi-cohort atrial fibrillation meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet; broad consortium-style training_development_cohorts) with a direct AF endpoint (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation) and strong reported discrimination in European evaluation (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus a per-SD HR ~1.67. Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., snpnet ‘813 traits’, UKB portability) which domain guidance penalizes when disease-focused alternatives exist, or use horizon-conditioned / risk-wrapper endpoints or clinical risk-calculator packaging (e.g., ‘5-year risk’, CHARGE-AF covariate inclusion) which is negative evidence for standalone PRS comparability. Remaining limitation: the reported C-index is a full-model metric with covariates including CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided for PGS005168 in this context, so confidence is reduced despite strong overall study/endpoint support.

All four candidates are direct matches in the sense that they include atrial flutter in the reported trait/EFO, but only PGS001263 is specifically labeled and phenotyped as “Atrial flutter” (endpoint fidelity advantage over the three “atrial fibrillation and flutter” composites, including one time-to-event definition). PGS001263 also reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates 0.02517), enabling a heritability sanity check; its PGS-only R2 is below the provided local h2_obs=0.0157 but the scale mismatch/interpretation is not fully resolvable from the context, so this is only weakly reassuring rather than definitive. However, confidence is limited because (i) PGS001263 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank “813 traits” sparse snpnet framework paper (a known weaker archetype for external generalization per the provided domain knowledge), and (ii) the alternative models from the “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” paper (PGS001841/PGS002050) are also framework-style and lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), making it hard to establish a clearly superior choice. Given the best endpoint alignment plus availability of PRS-only metrics, PGS001263 is the best-supported direct-match, but overall evidence remains insufficient for a high-quality designation.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS000327, PGS002790). PGS000327 has the strongest endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis, and it comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS publication (Nat Genet) with multi-cohort development. It also provides supportive PRS signal evidence via an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) and a reported R²=0.0245 (noting this appears to be a full-model R², but covariates are limited to genetic PCs and genotyping wave). In contrast, PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported: "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)") despite the ASD label fields, and its reported partial R² (0.00546) is weaker and less directly comparable. Confidence is Moderate because neither model reports clearly PRS-only (no-covariates) AUC/R², and PGS000327’s R² is not explicitly PRS-only.

All 20 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma). The strongest endpoint-fidelity cluster is the Cancer PRSweb (Am J Hum Genet, 2020-12-15) family with phenotyping_reported exactly “Basal cell carcinoma” and only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), avoiding explicit risk-wrapper or treatment-aware packaging. Within that coherent family, PGS000454 (P+T, 27 variants) has the best-supported performance among siblings with comparable endpoint/covariates: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), Nagelkerke R² 0.0489, and strong per-SD OR 1.661 (1.568–1.759) plus high top-1% vs rest OR 3.79 (2.68–5.35). Competing PRSweb siblings are slightly weaker on AUROC/R² and/or effect sizes (e.g., PGS000447/448 AUROC ~0.587–0.591; PGS000456 AUROC 0.63 but lower R² 0.0456; UKB-trained siblings AUROC ~0.611–0.617). Non-PRSweb alternatives either have weaker/less comparable metadata (PGS000119 reports AUROC 0.64 but from a different paper/family with only full-model AUROC and smaller validation; PGS000730 has unknown covariates; PGS003416/PGS003417 lack comparable discrimination metrics and have broader phenotyping_reported “Keratinocyte cancers”; PGS005207 is survivorship/treatment-context specific). Main limitation: none of the candidates report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², so ranking relies on full-model metrics and effect sizes under similar basic covariates, which lowers certainty to Moderate.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo including "bilirubin metabolism disease". PGS001824 and PGS002032 have the most endpoint-faithful phenotyping ("Disorders of bilirubin excretion") compared with PGS000924, which is a broader composite ("Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism") and uses a time-to-event endpoint (explicitly a warning signal in the provided domain guidance). Between the two bilirubin-excretion models, the visible evidence shows identical phenotype, covariates, training cohort (UKB), evaluation ancestry context, and the same partial correlation (0.0716) with overlapping CIs; thus performance does not differentiate them. Given the domain guidance that, when PRS-only AUC is absent across candidates, methodological properties and variant count become more reliable tie-breakers, PGS002032 (LDpred2; 19,768 variants) is structurally preferred over PGS001824 (penalized regression; 22 variants). Limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², and the only comparable metric for the selected model is partial-r, so the recommendation remains sub-optimal despite good phenotype alignment.

All three candidates are direct matches within the bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder, bipolar I, bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and similar variant counts (~935k–949k), leaving limited differentiating evidence. For the target trait labeled broadly as “bipolar disorder,” PGS002786 has the closest trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo both bipolar disorder) and comparable covariates (age, PCs1-3). However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields describe non-diagnosis outcomes (cognitive/behavioral measures) rather than bipolar disorder case-control status, and the only reported metric is a small partial R²/full_model_r2 (~0.0025–0.0031) without PRS-only AUC/R² or effect sizes, making strength and comparability uncertain. Given these limitations and the near-indistinguishable sibling set, selection is sub-optimal with low confidence.

All three candidates are direct matches at the broad target level via EFO mapping to coagulation-related disease entities, but none is a clearly high-quality, disease-focused PRS for the generic umbrella trait "blood coagulation disease" based on the visible evidence. PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (blood coagulation disease) and is the only candidate with explicit PRS-comparable discrimination metrics reported (including PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS R² 0.0578, plus a European validation AUROC record), which provides comparatively stronger performance evidence than the two congenital clotting-factor deficiency scores that report only partial correlation. However, PGS001033 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-model framework paper ("across 813 traits") and is extremely sparse (1 variant) with a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are warning signals for external generalizability and endpoint fidelity for a generic disease target. The alternative candidates (PGS001826, PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital deficiency phenotype (different EFO) and lack PRS-comparable AUC/R², making them hard to justify as better direct matches for the broad target. Overall, a direct-match exists but evidence is limited and conflicted, so confidence is low.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the provided context. Among the strongest direct breast-cancer endpoints, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is supported by: (i) clear phenotype alignment (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), (ii) strong reported discrimination within a coherent disease-focused benchmarking family ("Evaluation of polygenic scoring methods in five biobanks..."), and (iii) the best full-model AUROC among the comparable UKB-derived method-comparison set shown (AUROC≈0.6625 with R²≈0.0764; OR per SD≈1.83). It also uses covariates listed as 0, avoiding explicit clinical risk-calculator/family-history packaging that would inflate comparability. Main limitation: the context largely reports full-model AUROC/R² rather than explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² for most candidates (including this one), making cross-model performance comparisons imperfect; additionally, several other strong direct-match models exist (e.g., PGS000332, PGS000335, PGS004688) with different study designs and covariate sets, so the preference is evidence-based but not definitive.

All 10 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=celiac disease, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and availability of PRS-comparable performance. PGS001301 has acceptable phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Malabsorption/coeliac disease" explicitly includes coeliac disease) and, unlike most others, reports PRS-comparable metrics (performance_metrics.auc=0.82867 and r2=0.14224; also lists "PGS AUROC (no covariates)" and "PGS R2 (no covariates)"). Its PRS-only R2 (0.14224) is below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.2305), passing the sanity check. Competing disease-focused celiac-specific models (e.g., PGS000040, PGS000316) report only full-model AUROC (0.90 and 0.879 respectively) with unknown covariates, which domain guidance says should not be substituted for PRS-only performance; several UKB portability models (PGS001856/001894/002067/002107) provide only partial-r without AUROC/R2. Main limitation: PGS001301 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain knowledge flags as a generalization risk versus disease-focused studies, so confidence is reduced despite stronger PRS-comparable metric reporting.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Among them, PGS003428 is the most disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis-derived score (Hum Mol Genet 2023: “GWAS meta-analyses clarify genetics of cervical phenotypes and inform risk stratification for cervical cancer”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; ~2.9M variants), which is structurally favored over sparse/hits-only approaches when endpoint alignment is comparable. Its reported effect size is moderate (HR=1.33 per SD) with basic covariates (age, smoking), supporting meaningful PRS signal without obvious heavy clinical leakage. However, confidence is limited because the available discrimination metrics across candidates are mostly full-model AUROC/C-index (not clearly PRS-only), and PGS001299 is the only model reporting explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.55; PGS R2 ~0.0026) but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalization risk), making cross-candidate performance comparisons uncertain. Therefore, a direct match exists but the evidence does not support a clearly high-quality, unambiguous winner.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis at the disease level (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or a closely related composite endpoint including cholecystitis). However, most candidates lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (AUC/R²) and/or have endpoint/covariate ambiguities, limiting a clearly high-quality pick.

PGS001174 is preferred because it is an exact EFO match (cholelithiasis) with explicit PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.62342; PGS-only R²=0.02808) plus incremental AUROC (0.04311) and stated covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R² is also plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling context (h2_obs=0.0214; h2_liability=0.1372), supporting metric sanity. The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; additionally, its endpoint is time-to-event, which is a mild endpoint-design mismatch for generic disease-risk use.

Competing direct matches are not clearly stronger on visible evidence: PGS001861 and PGS002072 use a composite phenotype (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUC/R²); PGS004476 and PGS004546 are exact K80 cholelithiasis but provide only per-SD ORs (1.22 and 1.30, respectively—modest) with unknown covariates; PGS005150 is exact cholelithiasis but has EAS-only evaluation and reports only a beta without PRS-comparable discrimination metrics. Given these gaps, PGS001174 is the best-supported direct-match choice, but overall evidence remains insufficient for a high-confidence/high-quality designation.

Multiple direct-match CKD candidates are present (22 total). PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused (publication: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”, Nat Med), uses a clinically specific CKD endpoint aligned to the target (“CKD stage 3 or greater”, phenotyping: eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m^2), and includes multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/ASN/EUR/MAE) suggesting broader transportability than EUR-only evaluations. It also reports a per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65) consistent with moderate PRS signal. Main limitation: the reported AUROC (0.78) is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite strong endpoint/study alignment.

Direct-match COPD candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001783 is preferred because it is a COPD endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and, relative to the other direct COPD options shown, it provides comparatively stronger PRS-comparable evidence (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) and a reported AUROC (0.74, though this appears to be a full-model metric and is not directly comparable to PGS-only AUROC). Competing direct COPD models from the UKB ‘813 traits’ sparse snpnet framework (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334) explicitly report PGS-only metrics but these are weak (PGS-only AUROC ~0.54; PGS-only R2 ~0.002–0.003), and the domain guidance flags pan-trait sparse UKB framework scores as often underperforming in external validation. Other direct COPD candidates (PGS001788, PGS004466, PGS004536) either have weaker covariates-regressed-out R2 (PGS001788) or lack comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics and have unknown covariates (PGS004466/PGS004536), limiting interpretability. Overall limitation: the best-supported choice still has incomplete comparability because PGS001783 does not report PGS-only AUROC and comes from a global biobank framework-style paper, so the evidence does not support a clearly high-quality, unambiguous winner.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (cirrhosis of liver) are present (notably PGS000726 and PGS004621 with trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver; others are alcohol-related subtypes). PGS004621 is best supported on endpoint alignment (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both 'Cirrhosis') and structural/study evidence: a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with large variant count (1,089,806) and a large multi-cohort development/validation context (training cohorts listed across multiple biobanks; validation n=1,153,995; EUR evaluation). However, the evidence remains limited for a high-confidence pick because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination (the AUROC values shown are full-model/unspecified), making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; additionally, PGS000726 is also an exact EFO match with effect-size evidence but lacks comparable AUROC/R2, leaving meaningful competition.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the target EFO and sharing the same reported/phenotyped endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), same publication family (UKB portability framework), similar training/validation context (UKB; DEV EUR; EVAL EUR/SAS), and essentially identical reported performance (partial-r ~0.056 with overlapping CIs). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes available for either, performance evidence is limited and cannot strongly differentiate them. Under the domain-knowledge fallback when PRS-comparable AUC is absent, structural signals (method/variant count) become the main tie-break; PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (32,552 vs 45), which is a supportive methodological/coverage signal relative to the sparse penalized regression score. However, because both models come from a portability framework paper and the only available metric is a modest partial correlation, the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both aligned to the target with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = "Corneal dystrophy" and similar basic covariates and ancestry evaluation context from the same publication family. With endpoint fidelity and study context effectively tied, the main differentiators in the visible evidence are (i) PRS-comparable performance and (ii) structural/method signals. PGS002042 shows a higher reported partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) in the selected European validation record and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally supportive when other fields are comparable. Limitation: neither model reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect sizes, and both come from a UKB portability framework paper, so the evidence base is limited to partial-r plus structural metadata; this keeps confidence at Moderate rather than High.

Multiple direct-match candidates exist for coronary artery disease (trait_efo matches across many models). PGS003725 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is directly aligned to the target disease (“Coronary artery disease”), it comes from a disease-focused multi-ancestry CAD PRS study (Nat Med; “A multi-ancestry polygenic risk score improves risk prediction for coronary artery disease”), and it reports strong per-SD effect sizes (HR=1.75; OR=2.14) with a large validation sample (n=308,264) and multi-ancestry evaluation context. However, confidence is not high because many other endpoint-faithful CAD models are present (e.g., PGS000013, PGS000018, PGS002244, PGS003446), and for PGS003725 the context does not provide PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2); several competitors report full-model AUROC but those are not directly comparable and may be covariate-influenced, limiting a definitive ‘best’ choice from the visible metadata alone.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo=Crohn disease; phenotyping_reported is Crohn’s disease or a close ICD10/time-to-event instantiation). PGS004254 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with very large variant count (744,682) and reports a strong effect size (OR=2.18, 95% CI 2.05–2.32) plus a high reported AUROC (0.72, EUR). In contrast, PGS001330 and PGS001331 come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework (“across 813 traits”) with very small PRS-only metrics (PGS-only R² ~0.006–0.007; PGS-only AUROC ~0.576–0.579) despite large training/validation sizes, which domain guidance flags as a common underperforming archetype. Main limitation: for PGS004254 the available AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R² provided), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be directly compared to the snpnet models; this missing comparability evidence lowers confidence and keeps the outcome sub-optimal.

Direct-match dementia models are present (e.g., PGS000929, PGS000946, PGS001827, PGS002035, PGS004281–PGS004284, PGS004318, PGS005170). PGS005170 is the best-supported direct match because it has strong phenotype alignment to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia), uses an explicitly integrative/ensemble PRS construction (integrative PRS of 24 component PRSs), and reports a comparable discrimination metric (AUROC=0.761) plus an effect size (HR=1.25, 95% CI 1.11–1.42) with only basic demographic/PC/APOE covariates. Competing exact-label dementia candidates are either from pan-trait/portability frameworks with modest PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS000929/PGS000946 snpnet; PGS001827/PGS002035 portability partial-r) or have less clear PRS-comparable performance reporting (e.g., PGS004318 reports HR but no PRS-only AUC/R2). Confidence is not High because several dementia-labeled alternatives exist with different study archetypes and metric types, and the context does not provide head-to-head PRS-only performance across these candidates.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models mapped to depressive disorder / major depressive disorder). PGS003333 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is an explicit disease endpoint (“Major Depressive Disorder”), its trait_efo aligns (major depressive disorder), and it is derived from a disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS context (23andMe/PGC/UKB) using a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with large variant coverage (1,088,415), with reported validation signal (Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.022 in EUR, n=34,703). Main limitation: across the candidate set, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are largely absent and many reported metrics are full-model or otherwise non-comparable; additionally, some alternatives have endpoint/covariate mismatches (e.g., PGS000767 uses a brain imaging phenotype; PGS000907 is antidepressant side-effect context; PGS004885 is incident/time-to-event), so while PGS003333 is the most coherent direct disease PRS from the visible evidence, the overall evidence base does not support a high-confidence single best choice.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with generally coherent phenotyping_reported (Dilated cardiomyopathy / Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy / Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy). No candidate reports a clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R²; most reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model or otherwise not explicitly PRS-comparable, which limits confident ranking (per domain guidance not to substitute full-model AUROC as PRS performance). Within the most endpoint-faithful cluster for generic DCM risk (the ‘Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy’ models evaluated in EUR), PGS004951 (MTAG) is preferred over its non-MTAG sibling PGS004950 based on domain guidance that MTAG variants are mildly preferred within the same study family, and it also shows stronger reported metrics/effect size than PGS004950 (full_model_auc 0.67 vs 0.64; OR 1.93 vs 1.71). Competing MTAG models (e.g., PGS004862, PGS004947, PGS004949) have similar or slightly higher full-model AUROC in some cases, but differ in endpoint framing (non-ischemic vs clinical) and/or evaluation ancestry context, and the lack of PRS-only metrics makes these small AUROC differences unreliable for decisive selection. Therefore a direct-match exists, but evidence is insufficient for a high-confidence ‘best’ choice.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping_reported is a direct diagnosis endpoint for PGS004614 and ICD K57 endpoints for PGS004474/PGS004544; PGS000996 includes diverticulitis; PGS000997 is time-to-event). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS000997 reports higher PGS-only performance than PGS000996 (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 vs 0.552; PGS-only R2 0.01777 vs 0.00372) with similar basic covariates and same pan-trait UKB framework context, making it the best-supported choice from the available comparable evidence. However, confidence is limited because (i) PGS000997 is a time-to-event endpoint (a noted warning signal for generic disease-risk deployment), (ii) the strongest-looking disease-focused publication (PGS004614, Cell Genom) lacks PRS-only metrics and reports only a full-model AUROC with family history/age/sex covariates (not directly comparable to PRS-only), and (iii) the 2024 Commun Biol models (PGS004474/PGS004544) provide only per-SD ORs (~1.31–1.32) with unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics, preventing a clear high-quality winner.

All three candidates are direct matches for dupuytren contracture (trait_efo = Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported aligns). PGS001254 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.6646; PGS R2 0.0247) but comes from a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; its stronger full-model AUROC (0.7413) is not treated as decisive. PGS001880 and PGS002092 are from the same UKB portability framework paper (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores”) and lack AUROC/R2, but they provide comparable PRS-only evidence via partial correlation; among them, PGS002092 is slightly stronger (partial-r 0.0797 vs 0.0783) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (484,484 vs 2,443), a structural advantage when endpoints are otherwise identical. Overall, the best-supported direct-match choice is PGS002092, but confidence is limited because the top candidates are all framework/portability-derived and the two leading portability models lack standard PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUROC/R2), making the evidence base incomplete.

All four candidates map to the target EFO (follicular lymphoma), but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS002304 has coherent phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”) and provides the strongest available discrimination evidence in the context (full-model AUROC 0.61, European evaluation). By contrast, PGS000643/PGS000644 are labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” (near-synonymous with follicular/nodular per ICD10 C82 wording, but not exact), and their reported AUROCs are much lower (~0.53–0.54) with only basic covariates. PGS003455 has an internal metadata conflict (trait_reported/trait_efo indicate follicular lymphoma, but phenotyping_reported is “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”), making endpoint fidelity unclear despite a reported per-SD OR. Overall, PGS002304 is best supported on phenotype alignment plus available performance, but confidence is limited because the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 reported) and covariates are unknown, reducing comparability and interpretability of the reported performance.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant clinical subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), so a direct-match exists. Among the pool, PGS001792 (POAG; PRS-CS-auto) has a disease-endpoint phenotype (POAG), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method, and reports PRS-comparable performance (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.03209) plus a full-model AUROC of 0.777 in a large validation sample (n=347,396; European selected). Competing options either (a) come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., snpnet UKB models PGS001321-001323; portability paper PGS001836/PGS002043) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models, (b) rely on sparse GWAS-hit sets with weaker/less comparable metrics (e.g., PGS000350 OR 1.24; PGS002741 full-model AUROC 0.67), or (c) report only full-model AUROC with potentially non-PRS covariate contribution (e.g., PGS000137 includes family history; PGS004944 reports full-model AUROC 0.748 without PRS-only metrics). Limitation: the evidence is still incomplete for a ‘high-quality’ designation because most candidates lack clean PGS-only AUROC, and PGS001792’s AUROC is full-model (not directly comparable as PRS-only), so the selection rests on a mix of endpoint fidelity + method + a single PRS-comparable R2 rather than multiple consistent PRS-only discrimination metrics across studies.

Multiple direct-match gout PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS000199, PGS000711, PGS001248, PGS001249, PGS001789, PGS002030, PGS004160, PGS004265/4266/4269, etc.). PGS001248 is best supported from the visible evidence because it provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.66908 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.04014) alongside a direct gout endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Gout") and standard demographic/PC covariates, enabling interpretation of PRS contribution rather than relying on full-model AUROC. Competing candidates often report only full-model AUROC (not PRS-only) or effect sizes without PRS-only discrimination, making cross-model comparison less reliable; some also use endpoints like time-to-event (PGS001249) or specialized settings (e.g., arthritis outpatients in PGS000199). However, confidence is not high because several other direct gout models show similar full-model AUROC in European evaluation (e.g., PGS001249 full-model AUROC=0.81772; PGS001248 full-model AUROC=0.81572; PGS001789 full-model AUROC=0.807; PGS004265/4266 ~0.798), but many lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, so the evidence does not cleanly establish a single unequivocal winner across the entire candidate set.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry set and the same validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown, which domain guidance cautions should not be used as the primary ranking signal, and covariates are listed as Unknown for all, limiting comparability. Given these constraints, PGS005271 is modestly preferred because it shows the strongest supportive PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD ≈ 1.55, which is stronger than PGS005272’s ≈1.42 and far stronger than PGS005270’s ≈1.04) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with ~1.085M variants, which is structurally favorable versus the sparse P+T model (55 variants). Remaining limitation: the key performance evidence is not PRS-only and covariate details are missing, so the selection cannot be considered high-confidence.

Direct-match candidates for heart failure are present (multiple models with trait_efo=heart failure or congestive heart failure). PGS005097 is preferred because it is a disease-focused, multi-cohort heart-failure PRS (Nat Genet 2025; training cohorts include multiple major biobanks/consortia such as HERMES, MVP, FinnGen, etc.), uses a modern genome-wide cross-ancestry method (PRS-CSx) with a large variant set (1,274,692), and reports a validation AUROC (0.72 with CI) plus an additional metric (Brier skill score), supporting non-trivial discrimination. However, the evidence remains insufficient for a high-confidence ‘best’ choice because most candidates lack PRS-only (covariate-regressed-out) metrics, and the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates (age, sex, PCs), making cross-model comparability limited; additionally, several other direct-match CHF models report higher full-model C-index (~0.753) but are hard to interpret without PRS-only metrics and have smaller validation samples, leaving meaningful unresolved competition.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to hip osteoarthritis by trait_efo/labels, but the evidence is heterogeneous and often lacks PRS-comparable metrics. PGS002763 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: hip osteoarthritis) and provides a PRS-relevant effect size (OR=1.38 per SD, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), supporting a moderate standalone PRS signal. Competing models are either (a) framework/pan-trait UKB sparse score PGS000967 (snpnet; publication explicitly ‘across 813 traits’) where the high AUROC shown is full-model and the PRS-only metrics are modest (PGS-only AUROC 0.561; PGS-only R2 0.00628), or (b) proxy/treatment endpoints such as total hip replacement/hip replacement (PGS002728, PGS002750), or (c) newer models with unknown covariates and only single-point ORs without comparable discrimination metrics (PGS004478, PGS004548), or (d) an incident/horizon-style packaging context with only a full-model C-index (PGS004882). The main limitation is that PGS002763 still lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and is evaluated only in EUR, so the choice is best-supported but not high-certainty.

Direct-match candidates for Hodgkin lymphoma are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 and PGS003449). Among the PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease siblings with consistent phenotype alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both Hodgkin’s disease; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL; similar basic covariates age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) has the strongest visible validation performance (full-model AUROC 0.62; highest per-SD OR 1.476 with CI 1.154–1.889; highest reported pseudo-R² 0.0276) compared with PGS000638 (AUROC 0.601; OR 1.377) and PGS000637/PGS000640 (AUROC ~0.57; OR ~1.29–1.30). PGS003449 is also a direct-match by trait_reported/trait_efo, but its phenotyping_reported is inconsistent (listed as chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and it lacks comparable discrimination metrics, making it less coherent as a Hodgkin lymphoma endpoint. Limitation: all Hodgkin candidates here report only full-model AUROC/pseudo-R² (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), and the validation sample sizes are small (n=775 for PRSweb), so the evidence supports a direct match but not a high-certainty, clearly robust choice.

Direct-match hypertension PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS001320, PGS002047, PGS002652, PGS004234, PGS004236, PGS004934). Among these, PGS004236 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is explicitly aligned to hypertension (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both hypertension), comes from a disease-focused multi-ethnic hypertension study (Nat Commun: “A multi-ethnic polygenic risk score is associated with hypertension prevalence and progression throughout adulthood.”), and reports a relatively strong full-model AUROC (0.764) plus a substantial effect size (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21). Competing direct-match options either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., PGS001320 from the ‘813 traits’ UKB framework; PGS002047 from the ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores’ framework) or have weaker/less informative performance reporting (e.g., partial correlation only for PGS002047/PGS001838; AUROC-only with unknown covariates for PGS004934). Main limitation: PGS004236’s reported AUROC is a full-model metric with multiple covariates (including BMI and smoking), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution is unclear; therefore the direct-match recommendation is not high-confidence.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept of hyperthyroidism via either explicit hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis endpoints (PGS001042/PGS001043/PGS001815/PGS002023) or the clinically dominant autoimmune subtype Graves’ disease (PGS005264/PGS005265/PGS005266), which domain knowledge explicitly treats as a strong direct match for generic hyperthyroidism when alternatives are older UKB framework scores. Among the Graves’ disease models, PGS005265 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) and shows the highest reported AUROC among its close siblings (0.6652 vs 0.6637 and 0.6587) with the same validation sample size (n=94,651) and multi-ancestry evaluation context. However, confidence is limited because these Graves’ disease models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (no PGS-only AUROC/R²), making PRS-only comparability unclear; meanwhile the thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism UKB framework models do report PGS-only metrics but come from pan-trait/portability-style studies that domain knowledge warns often generalize poorly. This leaves a direct-match set with competing strengths and incomplete PRS-only performance evidence for the selected model.

All four candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = hypertrophic cardiomyopathy). Endpoint fidelity is strongest for PGS004910 and PGS004911 because phenotyping_reported is explicitly hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, whereas PGS000778 targets clinical events among pathogenic sarcomeric variant carriers (a restricted subgroup/prognosis-like endpoint) and PGS000739 reports a covariate-augmented full model including multiple clinical risk factors and rare-variant carrier status, making its AUROC less PRS-comparable. Between the two 2025 Nat Genet PRS-CS siblings (PGS004910 vs PGS004911), covariates and validation context are the same (basic demographics + PCs; EUR GWAS/EVAL; n=343,182), and the MTAG variant is domain-preferred when endpoint remains the same; it also shows stronger reported discrimination/effect evidence in the provided record (full_model_auc 0.80 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; higher HR/OR). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared across all candidates, lowering confidence from High.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo=hypothyroidism), but several have endpoint mismatches (e.g., therapy-induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients: PGS000759/PGS000761/PGS000820) or are from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., UKB 813-traits snpnet: PGS000965/PGS001181; UKB portability: PGS001816/PGS002024), which domain guidance treats as generally weaker than disease-focused models when a disease-focused alternative exists. PGS005218 is the most disease-focused, hypothyroidism-specific GWAS/PRS study in the set (publication title explicitly on hypothyroidism), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports strong discrimination in European validation (full-model AUROC 0.859 with CI) with a very large validation sample (n=441,692). Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates including thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), which domain guidance flags as near-outcome covariates that can inflate AUROC and are not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; PRS-only AUC/R2 is not provided here, so confidence is reduced despite strong endpoint alignment and study focus.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001823, PGS002031), both aligned to the target via identical trait fields (trait_efo="iron metabolism disease"; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported="Disorders of iron metabolism") and from the same UKB portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), covariates, and validation sample size. With endpoint and study context effectively tied, the only visible differentiator is performance: PGS002031 shows a slightly higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.1355 vs 0.1307). However, both models lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and effect-size reporting, and the publication context is a portability framework study, so the evidence base is limited and the performance gap is small—supporting selection of PGS002031 but with only moderate confidence.

All four candidates come from the same disease-focused publication family (Ann Rheum Dis; SparSNP; EUR dev/eval; basic covariates sex + PCs), so the primary differentiator is phenotype alignment to the target trait. PGS000114 is the only model whose trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are the broad target endpoint “juvenile idiopathic arthritis,” whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are explicitly subtype-specific (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular) and therefore are not as endpoint-faithful for a generic JIA target. Although some subtype models report higher full-model AUROC, domain guidance indicates full-model AUROC should not be used as the main ranking signal (and is not a substitute for PRS-only metrics), so the subtype AUROC advantage does not outweigh the endpoint mismatch. Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2, so confidence is based on endpoint fidelity plus consistent study/covariate context rather than directly comparable PRS-only performance.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to kidney cancer or near-synonymous renal carcinoma/renal cell carcinoma endpoints, with several explicitly using incident kidney cancer or malignant neoplasm of kidney phenotypes. PGS004908 is best supported in the provided metadata because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: kidney cancer; trait_efo: renal carcinoma), reports the strongest PRS-relevant effect size signal in the pool (OR per SD 1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58; domain guidance treats OR≥1.5 as strong), and also shows the highest reported AUROC among the listed models (0.74, EUR evaluation), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious clinical risk-calculator packaging. Main limitation: the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), and evaluation is EUR-only despite multi-ancestry GWAS; several other models have similar endpoint fidelity but weaker or less complete comparable performance reporting, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, notably PGS000708 (trait_reported/trait_efo: Kidney failure) and ICD-coded chronic renal failure models PGS004492/PGS004562 (trait_efo: kidney failure; phenotyping_reported: N18 Chronic renal failure). PGS000708 is preferred because its phenotype is explicitly kidney failure (though specified as 'Diabetic kidney failure in all'), it reports a time-to-event effect size (HR 1.19, 95% CI 1.13–1.26), and it provides a clear evaluation context (EUR) with basic covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs). However, confidence is limited because the only discrimination metric shown for PGS000708 is a full-model C-index (0.779) rather than PRS-only performance, and the phenotype restriction to diabetic kidney failure may not fully represent generic 'kidney failure'. The alternative kidney-failure EFO models (PGS004492/PGS004562) have unknown covariates and provide only OR effect sizes without comparable PRS-only metrics, making them hard to rank above PGS000708 from the visible evidence.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS002767 has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Knee osteoarthritis") and provides a PRS-informative effect size (OR=1.35 per SD, 95% CI 1.3–1.4), which is moderate discriminative evidence per the provided domain guidance and is more directly PRS-attributable than full-model AUROC values. Competing options have key limitations: PGS001192 is from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), and its reported full-model AUROC (0.645) is paired with small PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.5566; PGS-only R2 0.0068), suggesting weak standalone PRS signal; PGS002729 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.66) with covariates including BMI and lacks PGS-only metrics, so its AUROC is not directly comparable as PRS performance; PGS004479/PGS004549 have aligned gonarthrosis endpoints but only single-point ORs with unknown covariates; PGS004883 is incident-only and appears packaged for cumulative incidence with only a C-index (0.60) and small training n=404; PGS002749 targets total knee replacement (a severity/treatment proxy) rather than OA diagnosis and has limited validation evidence. Confidence is moderate (not high) because no candidate provides clearly comparable PRS-only discrimination (AUC/R2) in a disease-focused setting, leaving selection reliant on effect sizes and endpoint alignment with incomplete covariate transparency for several models.

All 5 candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = late-onset Alzheimer's disease). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence among them is for PGS000054, which reports an OR per SD of 1.73 (95% CI 1.57–1.93) in evaluation (AMR/Hispanic or Latin American), exceeding the domain-knowledge threshold for a strong effect-size signal (≥1.5). Its sibling PGS000053 is similar but has a weaker OR (1.29), and the remaining candidates either report only full-model metrics (e.g., PGS004918 AUROC 0.731 without PGS-only metrics) or have endpoint/phenotype ambiguity (PGS002289’s phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction rather than AD case-control). However, the overall evidence remains limited because none of the candidates provide explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², covariates are unknown for several models, and the best-supported effect size comes from a non-EUR evaluation ancestry while other candidates are EUR-evaluated—so the choice is not unequivocally high-confidence.

Multiple direct-match lung cancer PRS candidates are present. PGS000078 is the most broadly supported direct-match option in the provided metadata because it targets incident lung cancer (phenotyping_reported: "Incident lung cancer"), is EUR GWAS/EVAL (clear transportability context within EUR), has large validation sample size (n=392,539), and reports effect-size evidence (HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside discrimination metrics (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariate adjustment (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking variables/interactions), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided; per the domain guidance, this makes the apparent performance likely covariate-driven and not directly comparable across candidates. Other candidates either have weaker/less informative performance evidence (many report only full-model AUROC with varying covariates) or are endpoint-restricted (e.g., early-onset, never-smokers, or specific histologic subtypes), so they do not clearly surpass PGS000078 for a generic lung cancer target given the visible evidence.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple SLE and lupus erythematosus models). PGS000328 is preferred because it targets systemic lupus erythematosus with a clear lupus-focused endpoint (early-onset SLE) and reports relatively strong discrimination among the cleaner disease-focused candidates (full-model AUROC=0.83 in EUR, n=1,001). However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because (i) the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as unknown (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), limiting PRS-comparable interpretability, and (ii) several other direct SLE models exist with higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS003960 AUROC=0.89) but are penalized by explicit phenotype-risk-score covariate packaging, making cross-model comparison unresolved from the visible metadata alone.

Direct-match candidates for the target EFO term (lymphoid leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). PGS000077 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), uses a reasonably sized GWAS-hits set (75 variants), and reports supportive effect-size evidence (HR per SD 1.45, 95% CI 1.31–1.61) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), plus large European evaluation (n=391,338). However, confidence is not high because none of the direct-match models report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R²; the available AUROC/C-index values are full-model metrics and are not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance. Additionally, PGS000788 shows higher full-model AUROC and HR but is explicitly a reweighted/inverted-weights derivative of PGS000077 within a risk-factor integration/pan-cancer context, making its apparent advantage less clearly attributable to a better PRS rather than modeling/packaging differences.

All 7 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidentiary strength. PGS004606 is the most supported overall because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), comes from a disease-focused AMD genetics study (Nat Genet 2024), and provides supportive performance/effect evidence (full-model AUROC=0.71 with only basic covariates; OR per SD=1.76 [1.73–1.78]). Competing models are weaker on visible evidence: PGS001013 is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework and shows weak PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.553; PGS-only R2 ~0.006), while PGS001834/PGS002041 are from a UKB portability framework with only small partial-r (~0.016–0.018). PGS002269 has phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness proxy) and lacks comparable discrimination metrics. PGS004607 is from an AFR-GWAS-derived score but evaluated in EUR with lower AUROC (0.65) and smaller OR (1.48). PGS004952 reports a very high AUROC but only as a full-model metric with a small validation sample (n=1,232) and an apparent unit inconsistency in the catalog entry (AUROC shown as 84.2), making it hard to treat as reliable PRS-comparable evidence. Main limitation: for PGS004606 the reported AUROC is full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), so confidence is moderated despite strong endpoint fidelity and OR evidence.

Multiple direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS000079, PGS000118, PGS000732, PGS000743, PGS000766, PGS001304, PGS002246, PGS002247, PGS002253, PGS003430, PGS004795/004796, PGS004886, PGS005208). Among these, PGS002247 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo melanoma; phenotyping_reported: incident invasive melanoma), reports comparatively strong discrimination in European evaluation (full_model AUROC 0.691 with CI 0.661–0.722) and an explicit variance-explained metric (R² 0.072 with CI 0.051–0.10), and comes from an independent evaluation-focused melanoma PRS paper (Br J Dermatol) rather than a pan-trait portability framework. Main limitation: across candidates, many reported AUROCs are full-model (covariate-adjusted) rather than clearly PRS-only, making cross-model performance comparisons imperfect; additionally, several other direct-match melanoma models show similar or higher full-model AUROC in specific settings (e.g., PGS000743, PGS000813) but with different endpoints (familial melanoma) or smaller validation samples, so the preference for PGS002247 remains moderate-confidence rather than definitive.

All six candidates are nominally direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo for multiple myeloma (plasma cell myeloma), but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS003450 is explicitly misaligned (phenotyping_reported = chronic lymphocytic leukemia), making it a weak direct-match despite the myeloma label. Among the remaining models, PGS002281 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported = Multiple myeloma) and the strongest reported discrimination in a reasonably sized European evaluation (full-model AUROC 0.644, n=2,395) with basic covariates (age, sex, geographic region). PGS000653/PGS000654 are also endpoint-aligned and have larger validation (n=2,738) but materially lower full-model AUROC (~0.576–0.577) and only modest per-SD ORs (~1.32). PGS002306 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but is supported by a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and has unknown covariates, reducing comparability. Overall confidence is limited because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so rankings rely on full-model AUROC/effect sizes and endpoint/covariate metadata rather than directly comparable PRS-only metrics.

All 7 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, except PGS001271 which is explicitly time-to-event (still mapped to MS but less endpoint-aligned for generic disease status). Among candidates, PGS001270 provides the most PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC (0.65856) and PGS-only R2 (0.02904) plus incremental AUROC (0.08355) with basic covariates, enabling interpretation of PRS contribution; its PGS-only R2 is also plausibly below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1174), supporting metric sanity. Competing models either come from framework/portability papers with weaker or non-comparable metrics (PGS001831/PGS002038 only partial-r; no AUROC/R2), report only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics (PGS000809, PGS002726, PGS004699), or have an endpoint-type mismatch (PGS001271 time-to-event). Limitation: PGS001270 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; however, the disease-focused alternatives here lack PRS-only metrics, leaving residual uncertainty and preventing a high-confidence selection.

All listed candidates are direct matches to urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported consistently indicate bladder cancer / cancer of bladder / urothelial carcinoma). However, most models lack PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination metrics; many report only full-model AUROC or effect sizes, which domain guidance says are not directly comparable as PRS performance.

Among the direct-match set, PGS000613 (P+T; 15 variants; UKB-developed) is preferred because it provides relatively strong PRS signal evidence via effect size (OR per SD 1.301, 95% CI 1.227–1.379) and a strong extreme-tail contrast (top 1% vs rest OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.99–4.24) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch), and it is part of a coherent bladder-cancer-specific model family (Cancer PRSweb) with consistent endpoint/covariate structure. Competing siblings (e.g., PGS000611) are similar but slightly weaker on the visible tail-risk metric (top 1% vs rest OR 2.66).

Main limitation: the evidence remains sub-optimal because no candidate here reports clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2, and full-model AUROCs (including very high values in PGS000071/PGS000782) are likely covariate-influenced and not directly usable to rank standalone PRS quality per the provided domain guidance.

All five candidates are direct matches for urolithiasis via closely aligned endpoints ("Urinary calculus" with trait_efo=urolithiasis; or "Calculus of kidney and ureter" / nephrolithiasis/ureterolithiasis which are within the urolithiasis spectrum). Among the two exact urolithiasis-labeled portability-framework siblings (PGS001864 vs PGS002075), PGS002075 has stronger comparable performance evidence (partial correlation 0.0385 [0.0246–0.0524] vs 0.0323 [0.0184–0.0462]) with the same phenotype and covariates, and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with broad variant coverage, which is structurally favorable. However, confidence is limited because the best-supported alternatives include a pan-trait sparse UKB framework model (PGS001250) that reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 but is penalized by framework design and time-to-event phenotyping, and two newer nephrolithiasis-coded models (PGS004493/PGS004563) that report only modest per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28) with unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2—making cross-candidate performance comparability incomplete. Overall, PGS002075 is preferred but the evidence base is not strong enough for a high-quality designation.

Multiple direct-match candidates are present for the target trait uterine cancer, including exact-label uterine/uterus endpoints (PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS001795, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial carcinoma (PGS000075, PGS000786, PGS002300, PGS002735/36/37, PGS003381, PGS004244). Per provided domain knowledge, endometrial carcinoma is a strong direct match for uterine cancer (dominant subtype), so endometrial-cancer-labeled models are eligible and can be preferred if better supported.

PGS003381 is selected because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), uses a genome-wide method (lassosum) with a large variant set (529,365), and reports relatively strong full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.761; R² 0.11) with basic covariates (age, top 20 PCs), avoiding heavy clinical leakage. Compared with exact-label uterine cancer models, PGS001795 is a framework-style global biobank score with very small PRS-only R² (0.001948) and only moderate full-model AUROC (0.66), while PGS000541/542 and PGS003740 are sparse GWAS-hit scores with weaker discrimination evidence (AUROC ~0.57 or only OR reported). Main limitation: PGS003381 does not provide explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² (the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics), so comparability of performance across candidates is imperfect; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high.

All three candidates are direct matches to vitiligo by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity. PGS000738 has the most endpoint-faithful phenotype context (publication focused on autoimmune vitiligo/polygenic inheritance) and is evaluated in EUR with a reported pseudo R² (0.0386), which is below the provided vitiligo h2_obs ceiling (0.1738) and thus passes the heritability sanity check. PGS001536 reports explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”) and uses a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are warning signals for external generalizability relative to a disease-focused vitiligo study. PGS000760 is endpoint-mismatched: phenotyping_reported is anti–PD-L1–induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients (therapy-specific), so despite an HR=1.41 it is not a clean vitiligo disease endpoint. Overall, PGS000738 is the best-supported direct-match, but confidence is limited because its covariates are unknown and it lacks standard PRS-comparable AUROC/PGS-only metrics, while the only model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001536) carries a framework/time-to-event penalty.
